APPLICANT NAME: PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTH. - 2024 AND 2023 A2 SMALL DIA. LSLR PROJECT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Project will includes replacement of approximately 1,607 lead service lines, which includes an estimate 482 private lead service lines, 562 public lead service lines. Some customers will require both public and private side replacement while others will only receive either public or private replacement based upon where the lead pipe component is located.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The replacement of lead service lines will improve public health outcomes by reducing the amount of exposure to lead within the service area.

APPLICANT NAME: INDUSTRY BOROUGH MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY-WATER TREATMENT PLANT IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project proposes to construct a new ground water treatment plant. It includes cleaning of existing wells 1 & 2 and replacing two well pumps with new 10 horsepower (hp) pumps. The project also includes site improvements for a new treatment plant building and disinfection upgrades. This includes installing approximately 700 linear feet (LF) of waterline piping, constructing a new 40,000 gallon chlorine contact/oxidation tank with inlet static mixer vault, installing a 6,000 gallon hydraulic break tank to be used as storage tank for the distribution system and constructing a 2,200 square foot new water treatment building. The project also includes installing two (2) 40 hp vertical turbine pumps, a chlorine gas feed system, chlorine analyzers, fencing, driveway, electrical system upgrades, a new 175kW emergency generator with automatic transfer switch, a new SCADA system for effective control and monitoring of water system and all appurtenances associated with equipment installation and building construction.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Industry Borough Municipal Authority is currently under a Consent Order and Agreement with the Department for exceeding the maximum contaminant level for iron and/or manganese. Also, the current location/layout of the chlorine room does not comply with current Department regulations. The chlorine room is not isolated from other work areas; it is located in a shared building with electrical equipment and the workshop and does not have a separate ventilation system. Additionally, the existing well and treatment system does not have an emergency power source, resulting in unavailability of the water source during power outages. Finally, giardia disinfection contact time for groundwater rule compliance is accomplished using two contact tanks, one of the tanks is a buried steel storage tank that is in poor condition and at the end of its useful life.

APPLICANT NAME: FOXBURG AREA WATER AND SEWER AUTHORITY - WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The project consists of the installation of 6,500 LF of 6-inch diameter waterline, 300 LF of 4-inch diameter waterline, 700 LF of 2-inch diameter waterline, fire hydrants and appurtenances. The water treatment plant work consists of a new water treatment plant, four (4) greensand filters, chemical feed systems and miscellaneous items. The existing water storage tank will be replaced with a 150,000 gallon storage tank.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Foxburg Area Water & Sewer Authority has chosen to replace the aging waterlines and reduce their water losses. The water treatment plant’s existing building is not suitable for rehabilitation due to its construction and deteriorated state. In addition, the existing water treatment plant will not meet the Department’s drinking water standards. . The existing water storage tank is also in poor condition and beyond repair. Well No 6’s water quality is poor, but the Authority believes it can be modified and retained. The distribution system, consisting of cast iron pipe, has experienced multiple leaks, necessitating the replacement of many lines. In addition, there is only a single waterline that serves both the school and the business district. When leaks happen, these waterlines are shut down, cutting off water service to the key establishments in the service area.

APPLICANT NAME: PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTHORITY - 2025 SDWMR (LSLR)
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Lead service lines will be replaced with approximately 366 lead service lines among total 733 lines including an estimate 169 private lead service lines and 564 public lead service lines. Some customers will require both public and private side replacement while others will only receive either public or private replacement based upon where the lead is located. This project also includes around 170 PRVs, which is EPA defined "Green" for water savings.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The replacement of lead service lines will improve public health outcomes by reducing the amount of exposure to lead to the service area population.

APPLICANT NAME: MERCERSBURG WATER AUTHORITY – WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS, PHASE 2
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This water system improvement project includes abandoning the existing Buck Run water treatment facility and replacing it with a new greensand filtration facility. The new facility will treat water from the existing Buck Run Well with 50 gallon per minute capacity and the Zimm Well with 100 gallon per minute capacity using pH adjustment, oxidation and pressure filtration to remove iron, disinfection, and orthophosphate addition for corrosion control. The new facility, in conjunction with the Park Avenue well and treatment facility which are under construction, will allow the Authority to remove the Buck Run reservoir from service and continue to supply a reliable quality and quantity of water to its customers.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Mercersburg Water Authority (Authority) owns the Buck Run filter plant which treats surface water from the Buck Run Reservoir. The existing reservoir and filter plant are in need of major rehabilitation or replacement as evidenced by numerous violations of the Safe Drinking Water Act which were recorded in a Notice of Violation (NOV) dated February 26, 2020. The Authority entered into a Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department on September 10, 2020. This COA required the Authority to prepare an Existing Facilities and Treatment Alternative Study which outlined methods for compliance, the costs of those methods, and the Authority’s plan for achieving compliance. The Study concluded that the lowest cost, feasible compliance alternative was the development of a new groundwater source and the construction of two new water treatment facilities, the Park Avenue water treatment facility and the Buck Run water treatment facility. This alternative will allow the Authority to abandon the Buck Run Reservoir and existing filter plant.

APPLICANT NAME: PENNSYLVANIA AMERICAN WATER COMPANY - UNIONTOWN LSLR PHASE 1
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Project will include replacement of approximately 389 lead service lines as identified throughout the service area.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: To meet PADEP and EPA requirements, PAWC is required to replace all lead and lead impacted galvanized water service lines. PAWC has numerous lead service lines in the project areas and is working to replace the ones that we have currently identified.

APPLICANT NAME: MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY OF THE BORO OF WATERFORD - LEAD SERVICE LINE REPLACEMENTS - PHASE 1
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Municipal Authority of the Borough of Waterford will replace approximately 200 lead service. Services will be replaced in kind from the existing water main to the inside of the existing structure.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Currently, the Municipal Authority of the Borough of Waterford has 200 lead services, specifically with lead goosenecks, within the Borough of Waterford. Per The current Lead and Copper Rule promulgated by the Environmental Protection Agency, all lead services shall be removed by the end of 2034.

APPLICANT NAME: PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTHORITY - 2026B LSLR
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Based on PWSA's prioritization model run and following the previous Neighborhood LSLR Program 2023A, 2023B, 2024A, 2024B, 2025A, 2025B, and 2026A, PWSA estimates that this project 2026B will replace around about 3,274 lead service lines. The Service Area of this project are Allentown, Brighton Heights, Duquesne Heights, Elliot, Garfield, Greenfield, Manchester, Mount Washington, North Oakland, Point Breeze, Regent Square, Shadyside, Southside Flats, Squirrel Hill North, Swisshelm Park and a one-off 26B work order area.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: PWSA started efforts to replace public lead service lines in 2017 and included private lead service lines starting in early 2018. While great strides have been made in both corrosion control treatment (CCT) and Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR), much work remains. As critical as CCT is to water quality, the issue of lead in drinking water will not be resolved until all lead service lines are removed from the system. PWSA’s goal is to remove all lead service lines by 2026 - given the latest budget projections this has been extended to the end of 2027.

APPLICANT NAME: PENNSYLVANIA AMERICAN WATER COMPANY - PITTSBURGH LSLR PHASE 3 -DORMONT BOROUGH
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The replacement of approximately 575 lead service lines is proposed. The lead service line replacement (LSLR) work is planned to be conducted via direct replacement. The anticipated process includes excavating a small pit at the existing water main generally within the paved roadway and an additional small pit at the curb box generally near the roadway curb line. From those pits, a new water service line would be installed between the water main and the home.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: To meet PADEP and EPA requirements, Pennsylvania-American Water Company (PAWC) is required to replace all lead and lead impacted galvanized water service lines. PAWC has numerous lead service lines in these areas and is working to replace the ones that we have currently identified.

APPLICANT NAME: THE MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY OF THE BOROUGH OF PORTAGE - WATERLINE & METER REPLACEMENT PROJECT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The proposed project includes the installation of approximately 34,500 linear feet of water mains, approximately 15,700 linear feet of service lines, 24 fire hydrants, approximately 580 meter pits, and appurtenances by utilizing mostly open trench methods of excavation. Installations around railroad crossings and stream crossings will be completed by jack and bore to allow ease of replacement in the future, if required. The project also consists of replacing 6 identified lead and galvanized service lines and during construction, if any additional lead and galvanized service lines are encountered, the contractor will replace those as well.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Old, antiquated lines, exist in the system, many of which are nearing 100 years of service. This area has seen more breaks and leaks in recent months. Since the Authority has a high unaccounted water loss of 62.9%, this area seems to be a place to start water line replacement since it has a lot of older lines. As per a recommendation from the DEP, many of the meters will be removed from the structures and placed in meter pits at the property lines.

APPLICANT NAME: LEHIGH COUNTY AUTHORITY - ALLENTOWN LEAD SERVICE LINE REPLACEMENTS, CYCLE 3 - 2026
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project will replace lead service lines on the public and private side of approx. 1,000 services (City Census tracts 0700, 0800, 1900, 2100, 9700) within the City of Allentown. The project will include additional service line material investigations, installation of new service lines and appurtenances, and site restoration.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The existing infrastructure was installed in the late 1800s and early 1900s consisting of lead and/or galvanized lines. The replacement of lead service lines will improve public health outcomes by reducing the amount of exposure to lead to the service area population.

APPLICANT NAME: AQUA PENNSYLVANIA, INC. - UPPER DARBY LEAD SERVICE LINE REPLACEMENT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Aqua PA is seeking funding for the removal and replacement of approximately nine existing lead and 384 lead-impacted galvanized water service lines. The final number of lead and galvanized line replacements may be subject to change. The line replacements are expected to be performed in Delaware County within the municipalities of Upper Darby Township, Lansdowne Borough, East Lansdowne Borough, Millbourne Borough, and Yeadon Borough.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Aqua PA Main system (PWS ID # 1460073) supplies drinking water to customers within multiple municipalities in southeastern Pennsylvania. In an ongoing effort to reduce exposure to lead in drinking water for its customers in accordance with state and federal requirements, Aqua PA has been working to identify the location of customer-owned lead and lead-impacted galvanized water service lines (LSL) for replacement.

APPLICANT NAME: WESTERN BERKS WATER AUTHORITY -WATER TREATMENT PLANT IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The project includes additions and modifications to the Authority's water treatment plant (WTP) which will enable the facility to provide a long-term, reliable quality and quantity of water. A new sulfuric acid chemical feed system will be added so that the pH of the water entering the WTP can be regulated. The coagulant, fluoride, chlorine, polyphosphate, and ammonium sulfate chemical feed systems will be upgraded with new chemical feed pumps, storage tanks, feed lines, and appurtenances which will allow the Authority to treat water from Blue Marsh Lake during harmful algal bloom (HAB) events and when elevated levels of cyanotoxins, specifically microcystin, are present in the source water. The existing, outdated Greenleaf filters will be demolished and replaced with four new dual-media rapid rate gravity filters, each with a capacity of 2.67 million gallons per day (MGD). This will allow the WTP to operate at its maximum capacity of 8 million gallons per day(MGD) with one filter out of service. The existing clearwell will be baffled and a new 400,000-gallon clearwell will be constructed to enhance the resiliency of the WTP's disinfection system. Four new 1,800 gallons per minute high service pumps are proposed. Improvements to the sludge handling and processing systems will include a new 54,000-gallon backwash receiving tank, new sludge mixers and pumps, and an additional 3,000-square feet of sludge drying area. WTP's electrical, instrumentation, and process control systems will be upgraded to support the plant improvements.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Authority's water treatment plant (WTP) serves approximately 25,000 residents in Berks County, PA. The WTP is nearly 50 years old, and many treatment plant components have reached the end of their service life. The Authority has identified deteriorating chemical feed equipment, suboptimal filter backwashing, lack of operational flexibility in the clearwell, and insufficient sludge handling capacity as problems that need to be addressed in a complete WTP rehabilitation. Additionally, the emerging presence of harmful algal blooms (HABs) and cyanotoxins in Blue Marsh Lake present treatment challenges that the current WTP is not equipped to handle. Water quality data collected from Blue Marsh Lake between 2019 and 2024 showed that the average microcystin concentration was about 12.7-ppb and the maximum was 306-ppb. These are significantly higher than the EPA's 10-day Drinking Water Health Advisory Levels (HAL's) for microcystins, which are 1.6-ppb for school-age children and adults, and 0.3-ppb for bottle-fed infants and pre-school children.

APPLICANT NAME: CITY OF PHILADELPHIA - GEORGE'S HILL PUMP STATION
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project includes a new pump station at George's Hill Reservoir that will have the capacity to meet the typical peak daily demand of the Belmont High Pressure District at 21 million gallon per day (MGD) with six (6) pumps, redundant feed systems, standby generator, and on-site stormwater management. The upgrades to the existing Belmont station will include replacement of the pumps and interior modifications.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The new George's Hill Pump Station is required to provide redundancy to the Belmont High Service Pressure District and will draw water from the lower regions of West Philadelphia and pump it up to the northern section of this region. The existing Belmont High Pump Station must be upgraded to allow it to work in tandem with the new station. This critical infrastructure will improve functionality and increase resilience during emergency operations.

APPLICANT NAME: BUCKINGHAM TOWNSHIP -  HEARTHSTONE PFAS TREATMENT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The proposed treatment system will include a new building to house the proposed treatment system, air stripper, transfer pumps, granular activated carbon (GAC) filtration, and a backwash holding tank. The project will require an air stripper to reduce the radon that will be absorbed. SCADA controls will be installed to tie the PFAS system into the main control system. The project will be located at the Hearthstone Treatment Facility, which serves as a combined treatment facility for wells CS-3 and CS-4.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Buckingham Township Cold Spring System serves residents in the northern portion of the Township. Samples of water collected at Entry Point (EP) 102 for wells CS-3 and CS-4 have been analyzed for PFOA and PFOS. Analytical results indicate PFOS levels of 12.56 ppt and PFOA level o 13.31 ppt at EP 102. It was also determined that an air stripper will be required to reduce the radon level in the water which impact the carbon disposal. The radon level, while not excessive, would cause a higher level of radioactive carbon for disposal which could cause higher disposal or reconditioning costs for the carbon.

APPLICANT NAME: BOROUGH OF BRACKENRIDGE - WATER FILTRATION PLANT CONSENT ORDER IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The project scope includes: (1) Site piping improvements for the Clearwell and on-site distribution storage tanks to provide automatic shutdown capability isolating the Clearwell from distribution storage in accordance with Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department; (2) Flocculation and clarifier improvements for construction of a new flocculation tank with flash mixing, installation of new Lamella plate clarifier equipment inside of existing clarifier tank and demolition of exterior circular clarifier; (3) Repair and improvements to backwash equalization chamber and piping; (4) General electrical and control system improvements; and (5) Construction of an addition to the main building.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Borough entered into a COA with the Department on June 27, 2024, to improve the Brackenridge Water Plant. The COA required the Borough to perform site piping improvements for the Clearwell and install on-site distribution storage tanks providing automatic shutdown capability to isolate the Clearwell from distribution storage. Other improvements are being proposed as well.

APPLICANT NAME: NANTY GLO WATER AUTHORITY - WATER TREATMENT FACILITY UPGRADES
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Nanty Glo Water Authority intends to undertake a Water Treatment Plant (WTP) Upgrade Project. This project involves the installation of an additional filter and rebuilding the 2 existing filters, which will increase the overall capacity of the plant. The project will also include replacing the existing mixing manifold with a static mixer, installing a second backwash tank and an auxiliary plate settling vault, storage garage and the installation of all electrical, control, and plumbing equipment necessary to operate these new units and ensure compliance with environmental regulations. The project will also include several architectural & HVAC improvements to the building; the construction of a new garage to house equipment, materials and parts; and installation of an emergency shut down vault on the finished waterline downstream of the clearwell/tank. The absorption beds will also be cleared out to accommodate additional sludge storage.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Over the years, due to a combination of increased system demand and seasonal water quality issues with the Nanty Glo Water Authority (NGWA)’s primary source, the emergency interconnect with Ebensburg Municipal Authority (EMA) has been exercised more frequently than anticipated. NGWA’s current sources cannot meet minimum resiliency requirements for current water demand. If the existing reservoir source is compromised, the EMA interconnect would need to supply an average of more than 1 MGD based on the annual average daily demand for 2021 and 2022. Due to EMA’s current water supply obligations, EMA can only supply approximately 0.39 MGD through the interconnect for an extended period. Insufficient backup water supply not only makes NGWA vulnerable to any extended loss of their primary source in an emergency, but it also limits their ability to properly maintain their existing source and treatment facility. During poor water quality conditions, the throughput to the existing dual filters can be reduced by the addition of newly proposed third filter while maintaining filter run times between backwashes and still meeting system demand. There are also problems of NPDES discharge with the water reclamation system, so instead, all the wastewater has been discharged to the Class V injection wells. However, those have become inundated and overflow since the injection wells were only designed to receive the volume of the plate settler vault once per day to provide allocation for the solids to accumulate while limiting the quantity of water to infiltrate.

APPLICANT NAME: MADISONBURG WATER WORKS - CONTACT TIME PIPING
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project will install approximately 1,030 linear feet of 12-inch PVC piping in a serpentine configuration after the existing clearwell and prior to the existing water storage tank to allow additional chlorine contact time within the system before the water storage tank. A chemical vault will also be constructed before the water storage tank to accommodate a new chlorine analyzer and sample tap. Two new valves are also proposed during this project after the chemical vault, creating a blowff and entry-point shutdown before the water storage tank. Approximately 40 feet of 4-inch PVC piping will be installed after the valve vault, with part of that connecting into the existing piping to the water storage tank while the other part of that piping will serve as a blowoff location for non-compliant water.This project also includes the installation of approximately 400 linear feet of 1-inch PVC conduit for electric services to the chlorine analyzer as well as SCADA upgrades to the water treatment plant to be able to serve the new chlorine analyzer.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: This project will allow Madisonburg Water Works to correct the entry point shutdown requirement. During a PADEP inspection on May 16 and 17, 2023, PADEP personnel observed that the Madisonburg Water Works had failed to provide any entry point shutdown capabilities. This is violation of of the PADEP Regulations. A July 18, 2023 PADEP inspection report included a Notice of Violation for the MWW failure to provide any entry point shutdown capabilities, in violation of Section 109.602(i) of PADEP Regulations, 25 Pa. Code§ 109.602(i). On December 21, 2023, MWW was issued a fully executed Consent Order and Agreement between the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Department of Environmental Protection and the Madisonburg Water Works.

APPLICANT NAME: PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTH. - 2024 AND 2023 A2 SMALL DIA. MAIN REPL. (NON-LEAD)
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project will replace an estimated 49,710 feet of 4-inch and 16-inch water lines thus replacing older and undersized mains. 2023 Small Diameter Water Main Replacement – Contract A2, 2024 Small Diameter Water Main Replacement – Contract B, and 2024 Small Diameter Water Main Replacement – Contract C include the replacement of aging 4” to 16” diameter pipes with new zinc coated ductile iron pipe ranging from 4” to 16”. This work includes the replacement of water mains, valves, fire hydrants, and water service lines. Water mains were selected for replacement based on a number of risk-factors, including the prioritization of undersized mains, and mains with a history of break.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Due to the advanced age of the pipes, replacement of these mains will reduce the frequency of water main breaks, which will minimize the risk to public health caused by the resulting potential exposure to infectious diseases and will reduce the impact of unplanned water outages and street closures required due to emergency repairs. The replacement of older, leak prone mains will also provide for more efficient management of water resources by reducing the amount of treated water that is lost from the system. Furthermore, the additional volume of water that will be able to be delivered to areas with inadequate flow will reduce restrictions on development within the affected areas.

APPLICANT NAME: ALTOONA WATER AUTHORITY - HORSESHOE CURVE AND KETTLE WATER TP OZONE SYS. UPGRADE
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The existing ozonation systems at the Kettle WTP (one treatment train) and the Horseshoe Curve WTP (two treatment trains) will be replaced with new equipment including systems for liquid oxygen storage and preparation, nitrogen generation, ozone generation, gas injection, ozone destruction, and ambient gas monitoring. Additionally, the aluminum sulfate and sodium hydroxide bulk chemical storage tanks will be replaced at the Horseshoe Curve WTP.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Altoona Water Authority (Authority) operates six (6) water treatment plants (WTPs), all of which use ozone for the dual purposes of taste/odor control and oxidation of iron/manganese. Ozonation systems were first installed in each of the WTPs in the 1990s, and those systems started reaching the end of their design life after almost 30 years of use. The old systems are no longer manufactured and the Authority has found it difficult to acquire spare parts. The Authority has upgraded the ozone systems at the Mill Run, Plane Nine, and Tipton WTPs and upgrades at the Bellwood WTP are currently under construction. Similar upgrades are now planned for the Kettle WTP and the Horseshoe Curve WTP.

APPLICANT NAME: PA AMERICAN WATER COMPANY - BERWICK PFAS WTP
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project includes constructing a new water treatment plant (WTP). Raw water from the four wells will be conveyed from the Canal Street well site via a new pipeline to the new WTP. The WTP will have a buried clearwell, wetwell, and granular activated carbon (GAC) pressure filters. Disinfection and corrosion control will be included at the new facility. Sodium hypochlorite will replace the existing gas chlorine system. A corrosion inhibitor will be used, consistent with the current chemical used at the existing treatment site. The finished water will be conveyed from the new WTP to the existing distribution system via a new finished water transmission main.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The project aims to add the perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal capabilities at the Pennsylvania American Water Company (PAWC) Berwick facilities. Current well source has identified PFOA level of 11.5 ppt. The project will reduce the PFOA levels in the finished drinking water to the customers.

APPLICANT NAME: DOYLESTOWN TOWNSHIP MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY - NORTH WELLS #3 AND #4 PFAS TREATMENT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Proposed plans include construction of a new treatment building, which will house two Greensand Plus filters for removal of manganese, two granular activated carbon (GAC) filter vessels for removal of PFAS, and new chlorination and ortho/polyphosphate equipment. A new chlorine detention tank will be installed, as well as a 30,000-gallon aboveground holding tank to store PFAS media backwash water. This project includes removal of the existing well house, detention tanks, and related chemical feed equipment.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Doylestown Township Municipal Authority Main System (PWS ID# 1090128), referenced herein as DTMA, serves the townships of Doylestown, Plumstead, and Buckingham, as well as the New Britain Borough in Bucks County. DTMA has been monitoring perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in its water supply. Samples of water collected at Entry Point (EP) 107 has been analyzed for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS). Analytical results indicate exceedances of the PFOA Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) of at EP 107, as well as exceedances of the secondary contaminant MCL (0.05 mg/L) for manganese at EP 107. Water samples collected at Entry Point 107 for North Wells 3 & 4 exhibited elevated PFAS levels in 2024 and 2025, as follows averaged values): 12.7 ng/L PFOA and 7.2 ng/L PFOS. In addition, manganese has exceeded the state secondary MCL (0.12 mg/L averaged).

APPLICANT NAME: PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTHORITY - 2025 SDWMR (NON-LEAD)
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: 2025 Small Diameter Water Main Replacement C include the replacement of aging 4-inch to 16-inch diameter pipes with new zinc coated ductile iron pipe ranging from 4-inch to 24-inch. This work includes the replacement of approximately 15,000 ft water mains, 306 valves, 34 fire hydrants, and 366 water service lines. Water mains were selected for replacement based on a number of risk-factors, including the prioritization of undersized mains, mains with a history of breaks.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Due to the advanced age of the pipes, replacement of these mains will reduce the frequency of water main breaks, which will minimize the risk to public health caused by the resulting potential exposure to infectious diseases and will reduce the impact of unplanned water outages and street closures required due to emergency repairs. The replacement of older, leak-prone mains will also provide for more efficient management of water resources by reducing the amount of treated water that is lost from the system. In addition, the additional volume of water that will be able to be delivered to areas with inadequate flow will reduce restrictions on development within the affected areas. The water main replacement work will occur within the City of Pittsburgh and will benefit the existing population within the area.

APPLICANT NAME: MASONTOWN BOROUGH - WATER METER REPLACEMENT PROJECT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The proposed Project is to install exterior meter pits and replace meters at all service connections in order to reduce Borough water losses from the service connection to the customer water meter (currently located in the home).
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Water meters are currently located within the customer's house and therefore all water losses from the water main to the customer are borne by Masontown Borough. The intent of the Project is to relocate the water meter to the legal line of ownership.

APPLICANT NAME: GENERAL AUTHORITY OF THE CITY OF FRANKLIN - BARRETT FLATS WTP REPLACEMENT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Barrett Flats water treatment plant (WTP) project consists of constructing: (A) 3,700 square foot building housing one (1) set of finished water pumps (primary and standby) dedicated to pumping to the Miller Hill pressure district; (B) one (1) set of finished water pumps (primary and standby) capable of pumping to the City pressure district and accommodations for the future addition of one (1) set of finished water pumps (primary and standby) capable of pumping to the Oak Hill pressure district; and (C) a gaseous chlorine feed room, a polyphosphate chemical feed room, laboratory, restrooms, breakroom, and storage room. The WTP will also include two (2) new clearwell tanks with a total capacity of approximately 71,000 gallons, an emergency generator, and a parking area. Well water will be pumped to the clearwell tanks via a 12-inch diameter raw water main. Gaseous chlorine and polyphosphates will be added to the well water prior to the clearwell tanks via injection points on the raw water main. The water will be held in the clearwell tanks in order to achieve the appropriate contact time prior to being pumped.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Since the initial development of the Barrett Flats and 9th Street well fields, water quality at the 9th Street well field has degraded due to elevated levels of iron and manganese. Additionally, treatment and pumping facilities at the existing Barrett Flats WTP are not adequate to utilize the six (6) existing Barrett Flats wells. Also, a secondary Barrett Flats well field was developed but never permitted due to the limited treatment and pumping capacity of the existing Barrett Flats WTP. Additionally, the Water Supply Inspection Report from the PA DEP inspection conducted on July 24, 2024, noted that the existing building is becoming unsafe to work within as it has wooden floors that have rotted away, floor hatches that are rusting, and the pipes for the groundwater treatment are a tripping hazard. The report noted that these issues are a violation and recommended to pursue the WTP replacement as quickly as possible with operator's safety in mind.

APPLICANT NAME: CONEMAUGH TOWNSHIP MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY-METER PIT INSTALLATION PROJECT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Conemaugh Township Municipal Authority meter and meter pit installation project consists of approximately 2,200 new meter and pits in the water distribution system. Meter pits will be placed on the property line of each customer and connected to the existing service lines.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Conemaugh Township Municipal Authority has experienced high water loss (64 percent in 2023) and the existence of many long service lines that do not currently have meter and meter pits. Several meters are located within homes nd need manual reading wvery month. This project will reduce water loss and increase revenue for the Authority.

APPLICANT NAME: CHESTER WATER AUTHORITY - SUSQUEHANNA PUMPING STATION RELIABILITY IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The scope of the major station improvements is to replace the existing three constant feed pumps (Pumps #1-3) with 1,500 HP vertical turbine pumps with new variable frequency drives (VFDs); o Remove existing variable speed pump (Pump No. 4); Install a 2800 kW backup generator capable of running (2) of the 1,500 HP pumps on VFDs; replace the existing switchgear equipment and transformer; replace the existing 1,000 kW generator with a smaller power generator used for house power and SCADA reliability; remove hydraulic system on discharge valves and replace with combination electrical and individual hydraulic actuators capable of the necessary valve closing times during an emergency pump stop; remove unnecessary bypass and backflush piping; replace permanganate dry chemical system with liquid skid-mounted sodium permanganate chemical system with two (2) positive displacement pumps; demolish existing Chemical Building and constructing a new Chemical Storage Room next to the Pumping Station Building; replace existing control system equipment with up-to-date hardware and network infrastructure.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Chester Water Authority (CWA) is seeking funding for reliability improvements of their Susquehanna Booster Station. The Susquehanna Raw Water Pumping Station provides the only alternate source water to Chester Water Authority’s Octoraro Water Treatment Plant’s primary source water, the Octoraro Reservoir. In recent years, operational challenges have limited the station’s functionality. Some of the station’s components have reached their serviceable lifespan and are due for replacement. Other systems require upgrades to improve operational functionality and reliability. These improvements will provide increased station functionality and reliability with additional flow control, reduced maintenance, and improved emergency power systems. The project location will be within Fulton Township in Lancaster County; however, these facilities are permitted by the DEP Southeast Regional Office as the facilities serve customers in Chester and Delaware Counties.

APPLICANT NAME: THE MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WASHINGTON - WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Authority is proposing to replace the motor control center, raw water pump, and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system at its existing water treatment plant as well as the replacing approximately 15,000 linear feet of 6-inch, 8-inch and 12-inch diameter water lines. The project also includes the rehabilitation of the water treatment plant filters. Air scour will be provided through new underdrains within the filters. New filter media and filter troughs will also be provided as a part of the project.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Most of the equipment within the motor control center is outdated and reached the end of its useful life. If the motor control center failed, the Authority would not be able to produce water for a number of days. The Department has identified several issues with the filters, including loss of media and leaking troughs. Furthermore, the Department has recommended that the Authority add an air scour system to the filters. The SCADA system was installed on the water distribution system in 2006. Much of the control system equipment is now outdated. The Authority has also identified ten sections of water lines throughout the system that need to be replaced. Most of these water lines are 2-inch diameter, which is not properly sized for fire hydrants. Additionally, this reduced line size results in higher pumping costs to the Authority. These water lines also have a history of breaks which cause water outages to the Authority’s customers as well as excessive and costly damages to public roads and private property.

APPLICANT NAME: HIGHLAND SEWER AND WATER AUTHORITY - CROYLE WATER LINE PROJECT CONTRACT 2025-W-03
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Highland Sewer and Water Authority (HSWA) is proposing the Croyle water line improvement project located in Cambria County. The third phase called Contract 2025-W-03, includes installation of 51,000 linear feet (LF) of transmission and distribution waterline with all necessary appurtenances within Croyle Township, East Taylor Township, and Cambria Township. Work includes the installation of water line, water service line from the water main to the property line, and water appurtenances necessary for the system. Three new pressure relief valve (PRV) vaults are to be added to the system to reduce dangerous pressure levels that currently exist within the Croyle Township main lines. The project will also include the installation of new meter pits and residential service meters for all Croyle customers along the alignment to modernize metering and allow for better integration into the HSWA system.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: Highland Sewer and Water Authority (HSWA) owns and operates a water treatment plant and public water distribution system which serves over 10,000 customers in 17 different municipalities within Cambria County, PA. Additionally, HSWA sells “bulk” water to 13 smaller water utility owners which distribute and re-sell water to their customers. One of these utility owners is Croyle Township Water Authority (CTWA) (which servers 4 different municipalities). CTWA purchases all their water from HSWA. Due to difficulties managing and maintaining a public water system, CTWA is proposing to transfer ownership and operation of their water system to HSWA. Ownership will be transferred to HSWA, and HSWA will take over billing for these customers. There will be no interruption of service or changes in water quality because of this transfer. Prior to assuming ownership, HSWA is proposing many of the older or problematic water lines be replaced within the CTWA system. The pipes and appurtenances within the system are past their anticipated useful life and are prone to breaks and water loss. The additional tanks and pump stations will also improve water pressure conditions as well as the longevity and serviceability of the system.

PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Highland Sewer and Water Authority (HSWA) is proposing the Croyle waterline improvement project located in Cambria county. This second phase, called Contract 2025-W-02, includes the installation of 45,000 linear feet (LF) of water line, water service lines from the water main to the property line, and water appurtenances necessary for the system. The project will also include the installation of new meter pits and residential service meters for all Croyle customers to modernize metering and allow for better integration into the HSWA system.

APPLICANT NAME: WINDBER AREA AUTHORITY - MINE 40 WATERLINE REPLACEMENT PROJECT
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: This project primarily consists of the installation of approximately 9,650 LF of new 6-inch diameter through 12-inch diameter water distribution piping as well as associated infrastructure for both distribution piping and water service connections to approximately 224 users. Water service connection infrastructure is anticipated to include water service lines, appurtenances, and meter pits. The existing Authority-owned water service piping will be replaced to the customers’ private property line as part of the project. Work will in most cases end at the private property lines; however, several sections of Authority-owned service lines need to be replaced within private property boundaries. Easements will be obtained for these sections as needed.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The existing waterlines within the Mine 40 Area are a mixture of 120-year old 4-inch cast-iron pipe and approximately 40-year-old asbestos cement pipe. Most service lines in this area are composed of approximately 70-year old copper line. There are some 100-year old galvanized service lines present as well. Line breaks and reduced fire flow rates are an issue. In addition, Scalp Level Borough’s upcoming Sanitary Sewer & Storm Sewer Rehab/Separation Project is in the same project area and anticipated to put additional stress on the existing lines. The new sewer lines will cross the existing water lines in many locations. Water loss is also an issue system-wide. No lead service lines are known to exist within the project area.

APPLICANT NAME: KLINE TOWNSHIP MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY -SNYDER AVE WATERLINE
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: The Snyder Avenue Water Main Replacement project consists of approximately 4,200 LF of water main replacement along Snyder Avenue, Marcus Street, Bayview Terrace, and Hillside Road in Kline Township, Schuylkill County, PA. The existing water mains are small diameter, primarily 4-inch asbestos cement pipe, with some sections of 2-inch and 3-inch steel pipe located through private property. The proposed improvements will replace these lines with an 8-inch diameter water main installed within public rights-of-way. The project will also include fire hydrant replacement as well as replacement of existing water service lines, many of which are galvanized steel. This area has historically experienced a high frequency of service line failures and leaks, which will be addressed through this project.
PROB. DESCRIPTION: The Snyder Avenue project addresses aging and undersized water mains that are prone to leaks, failures, and service disruptions. Portions of the existing system are located on private property and consist of outdated materials that contribute to ongoing maintenance issues and reduced reliability. These conditions also limit the effectiveness of fire protection in the area. The project will correct these deficiencies by replacing the deteriorated infrastructure and relocating the system into public rights-of-way.

APPLICANT NAME: HIGHLAND SEWER AND WATER AUTHORITY - CROYLE WATER LINE PROJECT CONTRACT 2025-W-01
PROJ. DESCRIPTION: Highland Sewer and Water Authority (HSWA) is proposing the Croyle Water Project. The project is located in Cambria Township, Croyle Township, East Taylor Township, Jackson Township, and Summerhill Borough, Cambria County, Pennsylvania. HSWA is proposing to complete a water system improvement that includes the addition and replacement of all necessary appurtenances within the Beaverdam system through multiple phases. For the first phase (called as Contract 2025-W-1), the project consists of the installation of three water storage tanks and three pump stations (two new water tanks and a pump station will be added to the system; A tank and two existing pump stations will be also replaced) as well as all appurtenances and site work necessary to complete these installations and connection to the proposed waterline to be installed under the applications of future phases.

Additionally, HSWA sells “bulk” water to 13 smaller water utility owners which distribute and re-sell water to their customers.
